summary: Dedicated pool: snapshotter I/O bursts causing GPU attach delays, autoscaler misfires and throughput collapse
description: Issue summary: NimbusAnalytics observed repeated midday throughput collapses in their dedicated GPU pool. Impact: p99 latency spiked to >30s for batched routes, sustained loss of throughput for ~10-30 minute windows causing user-facing errors and retries. Initial triage indicated GPU attachments were delayed and autoscaler returned fewer slots than expected. Hypothesis: background snapshotter process is generating NVMe IO bursts on hosts used by the dedicated pool, causing IO wait and delaying GPU attach syscalls which the autoscaler interprets as node unavailability.
impact: Customer-facing inference requests experienced 20-70% throughput reduction during affected windows; timeouts increased and errors surfaced in SDKs. Billing/usage accuracy impacted for the window. Customer SLAs at risk.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run sustained small-stream batched workload against dedicated pool (NimbusAnalytics tenant) during midday window
2) Trigger a background snapshot job (internal snapshotter) that performs concurrent nvme writes on the same host set
3) Observe increased GPU attach latency and autoscaler reducing attaches/failing to meet demand
4) Reproduce p99 latency spike and throughput drop within 5-15 minutes of snapshot start
logs: 2026-03-12T12:04:09Z node/host-7 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector=...
comments: Support (Aisha): Initial triage suggests correlation between snapshotter background runs and observed attach latencies. Opened host-level IO dashboard (dash/host-io) and alerted infra.
SRE (Marco): Confirmed NVMe write stalls on host-7 and host-8 coinciding with the window; kernel iowait jumped to 78%.
Customer (Nimbus Ops - Raj): We started seeing spikes around 11:55 and it impacted multiple inference endpoints. We can schedule maintenance windows if snapshotting needs throttling.
Support (Aisha): Applied temporary mitigation: throttled snapshotter job parallelism for Nimbus tenant and pinned them to a different host-affinity group. Monitoring for stabilization.
SRE (Marco): Creating PR to add rate-limiter to snapshotter and to feed nvme/io-wait metric into autoscaler as a soft-signal (see PR #4821).
investigation_notes: Host IO dashboard shows repeated 20-40s spikes in nvme latency during snapshot windows; these align with attach syscall latencies recorded by scheduler.

Sampler traces from serving-runtime show batch workers blocked on cudaDevicePrimaryCtxRetain for durations that match kernel-level IO wait spikes — suggests attachment blocked by host-level resource contention.
Autoscaler currently only watches attach errors and node health; it treats prolonged attach latency as node absence which triggers conservative shrink decisions causing shortfall.
Noise isolation: the snapshotter runs were scheduled on the same GPUs' hosts due to affinity packing; other tenants on the same pool experienced collateral throughput loss (noisy-neighbor).
root_cause: Background snapshotter jobs performed unthrottled NVMe writes on dedicated pool hosts. The resulting IO saturation produced kernel iowait spikes which delayed GPU attach operations. The autoscaler misinterpreted attach latency as reduced capacity and reduced attaches, creating a feedback loop and customer throughput collapse.
resolution: Applied immediate mitigations and implemented medium-term fixes.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-12 13:00Z): Reduced snapshotter parallelism for NimbusAnalytics and moved active snapshot jobs off the customer's dedicated host affinity set. Observed restoration of attach latency to baseline within two attach windows and throughput returned to 95% within 12 minutes.
Short-term follow-up (planned rollout 2026-03-15): Deploy snapshotter rate-limiter and introduce host-tagging to avoid co-scheduling heavy snapshot IO with latency-sensitive dedicated pools.

Long-term fix (roadmap Q2 2026): Feed host-level nvme/io-wait metric into autoscaler heuristic so the autoscaler distinguishes slow attach due to IO from actual node loss; improve scheduler backoff policy to avoid aggressive pool shrinking on transient attach latency.
workaround: Throttle snapshotter parallelism to 1 job per host for tenants in latency-sensitive pools
Temporarily change NimbusAnalytics host-affinity tag to 'isolated-snapshot-avoid'
If immediate relief needed, move tenant to a warm spare dedicated pool with different host set
postmortem_actions: 1) Merge PR #4821 to add snapshotter rate-limiting and backpressure (owner: Marco)
2) Create autoscaler change to incorporate nvme/io-wait as a soft-signal (owner: infra/auto-scale team)
3) Update runbook: 'dedicated-pool-noisy-io' with playbook steps to identify and mitigate snapshotter collisions
4) Schedule a capacity isolation policy review for Q2 to reduce shared host IO between snapshot-heavy workloads and low-latency pools
follow_up: Notify NimbusAnalytics when PR is merged and when autoscaler change is staged; schedule a 1:1 postmortem with customer and infra for April capacity planning.
status_update: Mitigation applied and customer throughput stabilized. Engineering working on PR for snapshotter rate-limiter; autoscaler heuristic change scoped and planned. Monitoring active for 72 hours.
